description: Desktop app that records your on-screen work session and uses the GitHub Copilot SDK to reconstruct it as an intent + ordered steps, then builds a reusable Skill or Automation for Microsoft Autopilots like Scout, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, or Copilot Studio.

latest_release.name: Skill Recorder v0.9.1
latest_release.body:
## Source-only release

Skill Recorder 0.9.1 is published from commit
[`21bcc5ea48e8c8aa8730e8272bff3d1b1bab9e4d`](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/commit/21bcc5ea48e8c8aa8730e8272bff3d1b1bab9e4d).

This release is **source-only**. No installers or portable binaries are attached.
GitHub's generated archives contain the tagged repository source only.

## Fix

**Keep using an existing GitHub login after upgrading.** If no AI connection
preference has been saved yet, Skill Recorder now checks the existing Copilot CLI
authentication and automatically selects GitHub when already signed in.
Users upgrading from 0.8.0 no longer need to choose their connection again just
because the new BYOM setting was introduced.

- Existing credentials are reused in their original location; they are not
  copied, deleted, or replaced.
- Saved GitHub or BYOM choices remain authoritative. Forgetting a BYOM key does
  not silently switch the user back to GitHub.
- Users without an existing login still see the GitHub/BYOM chooser. Both
  options remain available through **AI connection** in Sessions.
- The migration check is bounded, runs once per app lifetime, and is coordinated
  with explicit setup and shutdown. A failed check displays a safe warning and
  leaves manual setup available.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Re-run the commit-pinned source installer below to update.
- This patch does not recover deleted or expired credentials. If the existing
  GitHub login cannot be verified, choose GitHub authentication to retry.
- Dependencies and installer scripts are unchanged. BYOM provider setup,
  key storage, privacy protections, and billing behavior remain as documented
  in [v0.9.0](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/releases/tag/v0.9.0).
- Locally assembled source builds are not redistributable release binaries.

## Validation

- 298 local unit/regression/import tests passed, including upgrade restoration,
  existing provider preferences, failure handling, concurrent setup, and shutdown.
- The actual bundled SDK/CLI BYOM image/tool transport and credential-persistence
  fixture passed without GitHub authentication.
- Production build, application/eval type checks, lockfile portability, and a
  285-package license inventory passed.
- Exact release-commit CI passed on [Windows x64/ARM64](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/actions/runs/43224062944)
  and [macOS/Ubuntu](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/actions/runs/43224063355),
  covering commit-pinned source installation, license/compliance checks,
  tests, builds, BYOM runtime transport, and applicable packaging/architecture
  checks.

## Installer script SHA-256

These hashes were calculated from the exact release commit's Git blobs.

```text
7678f7f8d38d600f2fb732f95afeadc8aa4f9b9802989d26e2f932970795770c  install.ps1
bd8b5200a2c140c5a5ed9299d565ac72cee5420181774008977eaf75f210db1d  install.sh
```

## Commit-pinned installation

### Windows 11 x64 or ARM64

```powershell
$commit="21bcc5ea48e8c8aa8730e8272bff3d1b1bab9e4d"; $env:SKILL_RECORDER_COMMIT=$commit; irm "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/$commit/install.ps1" | iex
```

### macOS or Ubuntu

```sh
commit="21bcc5ea48e8c8aa8730e8272bff3d1b1bab9e4d"; curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/$commit/install.sh" | SKILL_RECORDER_COMMIT="$commit" bash
```

For script inspection and hash verification before execution, use the
[inspect-first instructions](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/blob/21bcc5ea48e8c8aa8730e8272bff3d1b1bab9e4d/INSTALL.md#inspect-first-installation).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/compare/v0.9.0...v0.9.1

detail.readme:
# Skill Recorder **Record yourself doing a task once, then turn it into a skill your AI agent can repeat.** > [!TIP] > **Want to install Skill Recorder? [Go to the latest release](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/releases/latest).** > Scroll to **Commit-pinned installation** and copy the complete command for your > operating system. It is ready to paste: you do not need to edit it or download > the source code yourself. [Step-by-step instructions below](#install-it). Skill Recorder captures a real work session on your screen: the clicks, the app and window switches, the pages you visit, commands/output from its optional recorded terminal, and (if you want) your spoken narration. It then uses the **GitHub Copilot CLI** to reconstruct *what you actually did* as a clear **intent plus an ordered list of steps**. From there, one step turns that single run into something an agent can reuse: - a **Skill**: a `SKILL.md` procedure an agent runs on demand, or - an **Automation**: the same procedure on a schedule or trigger. Both prefer the agent's **native tools** (like the `gh` CLI or `web_fetch`) over replaying UI clicks, and generalize from your one example, so recording yourself submitting *one* form can teach the agent to submit *all* of them.

  

## How it works 1. 🔴 **Record.** Hit record (or `⌘⇧R` / `Ctrl+Shift+R` from anywhere) and just do your task. Skill Recorder captures your screen and activity locally, in the background. 2. 🎛️ **Control.** While recording, a small always-on-top bar shows capture, microphone, and recorded-terminal state. Open the session-scoped terminal, mute, unmute, or switch mics, then finish or discard with confirmation. 3. 🧠 **Analyze.** Click Analyze and your selected AI provider reconstructs one overall intent and an ordered list of steps. Review and edit until it reads right. 4. ✨ **Create.** From an approved analysis, generate a reusable **Skill** and/or a scheduled **Automation**. For skills, **Review SKILL.md** optionally shows the complete, read-only file text (including frontmatter) before installation or export. Preparing a preview writes no skill files. Close and reopen it without regenerating; Add/Export from either surface uses that exact preview. Editing the plan discards the preview. You can still choose Add/Export directly without reviewing or adding a confirmation step. Review provides visibility into the generated instructions, not a security guarantee. ### Import an existing recording Instead of recording your screen, use the smaller **folder icon beside Record** to choose a local **MP4 or WebM** file, such as a downloaded Teams demonstration. Chromium checks the actual video and audio before the details screen opens. Unsupported codecs, encrypted or unsupported track layouts, corrupt media, and files outside the import limits are rejected with an explanation. No converter, standalone FFmpeg installation, or additional codec download is required. The initial limits are **512 MiB**, **15 minutes**, and **3840 x 2160 pixels** (or an equivalent pixel count). Audio must be mono or stereo at no more than 48 kHz. Import supports one video track and at most one audio track. MP4 track types recognized are AVC, HEVC, VP9, or AV1 video with AAC/Opus audio; WebM recognizes VP8, VP9, or AV1 with Opus/Vorbis. Recognized track metadata is not a codec-support guarantee: the shipped Chromium runtime must actually decode it. Import memory use is higher than the compressed file size. A Windows ARM64 stress check with a 512 MiB input, 15-minute stereo audio, and the existing Whisper model resident peaked at approximately **4.6 GB (4.25 GiB)** across Electron processes. This is a measurement, not a guarantee for every file or platform, and excludes other apps and the external Copilot CLI process. The import decoder has a **2 GiB** working-set guard; recordings that exceed it are rejected even when their file size is within the limit. After validation, you can enter **Additional details**, or leave the field empty. Explain the task, supplement what is visible, or indicate where the demo happens. **Timestamps are guidance, not trimming:** other parts of the recording may still be processed. Choose the recording's spoken language when it contains audio. Analyze transcribes audio locally using the existing Whisper model (with the first-use download disclosed before proceeding); transcription failures stop the import's analysis so you can retry. Videos without audio and recordings with no detected speech are supported. The resulting activity list uses the normal review flow: edit details, reorder, add or remove activities, then create and review your skill as usual. Imported analysis uses frames, speech, and your details, not captured OS events; it cannot recover hidden clipboard contents or commands that were never visible or spoken. The original file is untouched. A local copy and derived artifacts are stored in Sessions, and deleting the session removes only that copy. Selecting a file does not send it to the cloud. Choosing Analyze sends selected frames, transcribed speech, and your details through the existing privacy-protection pipeline to your selected AI provider. Debug exports include the imported media and details, just as they include private data from live recordings. Only import recordings you are authorized to use, and keep sensitive/confidential content out of them. Live recording, its permissions and settings, and its event-first analysis are unchanged. Imports do not require microphone or screen-capture permission. For development, `npm test` includes the import contract/privacy tests. `npm run test:import:runtime` uses the reviewed Electron runtime to generate synthetic MP4/WebM files with Chromium and exercise decoding, seeking, silent and absent audio, unsupported codecs, cancellation, and source-file preservation. Run that check on each release target; it does not replace checking representative Teams files. Add `-- --large` to also import an exact 512 MiB synthetic MP4 and check rejection of a file one byte over the limit; this check needs additional memory and temporary disk space. The initial local measurements and runtime check were performed on Windows ARM64; other platforms and real meeting recordings require their own verification. ## Get started Skill Recorder is published as a **source release**: one command downloads a pinned Node.js runtime, builds the exact release commit on your machine, and adds a **Skill Recorder (Source)** app you can relaunch anytime. Nothing is installed globally. You'll need either a GitHub account with **Copilot access**, or a supported model provider's API key; the Copilot CLI ships with the app and powers both options. macOS is the primary target. Windows 11 (x64 and ARM64) is supported too (see [`WINDOWS-VALIDATION.md`](WINDOWS-VALIDATION.md)). ### Install it Open the **[latest release](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/releases/latest)** and follow these steps: 1. On the release page, scroll to **Commit-pinned installation**. Find **Windows 11 x64 or ARM64** or **macOS or Ubuntu**, then copy the **entire command** in that section using the copy button at the top-right of the code block. 2. Open **PowerShell** from the Windows Start menu, or **Terminal** on macOS or Ubuntu. Paste the command and press **Enter**. 3. Keep that window open while installation completes. The installer downloads what it needs, builds the app on your computer, creates shortcuts, and launches Skill Recorder. The first installation can take several minutes. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Copy the command from the release page, not a template from the technical docs.** > The release command already contains the correct version identifier; there is > nothing to replace. Do not paste commands containing > `<40-character-release-commit>` literally. > You do **not** need Git, a separate Node.js installation, or the **Manual developer > setup** instructions. The **Source code (zip)** and **Source code (tar.gz)** links > under **Assets** are not app installers. To review the script before running it, follow the release page's **inspect-first instructions** instead. Installation remains subject to your organization's policies. **Open it again later:** use **Skill Recorder (Source)** on your Windows desktop or Start Menu; on macOS, find it in `~/Applications`, Spotlight, or Launchpad; on Ubuntu, use the matching application entry. You do not need to reinstall each time. Advanced options, including running in the background on macOS or Ubuntu, are in [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md#commit-pinned-one-line-installation). ### Then record 1. **Grant Screen Recording.** On first launch, macOS asks for Screen Recording permission; grant it and you're ready to record. 2. **Record, Analyze, Create.** Do your task, then Analyze. When no AI connection is configured, an existing GitHub Copilot login is recognized and reused automatically, including after an upgrade from 0.8.0. Otherwise, choose **Bring your own model** or **GitHub authentication** the first time AI is needed. Both options remain available to everyone, including Microsoft FTEs, through **AI connection** in Sessions. Recording needs neither. If you choose GitHub, Skill Recorder reuses a valid login or offers sign-in. Finish authorization in your browser; the app verifies sign-in and automatically retries the interrupted analysis once. There is no login terminal window to close. Canceling sign-in or leaving that analysis prevents the automatic retry. On Windows, a local Microsoft Entra tenant hint can offer a choice between **Microsoft Enterprise SSO** and a **Personal GitHub account**. This is only a routing hint, not proof of employment. Microsoft sign-in has two separate steps: finish SSO in the browser, then authorize the GitHub Copilot app. When SSO lands on `github.com/enterprises/microsoft`, close that tab, return to Skill Recorder, and choose **Authorize Copilot**. SSO alone does not authorize the app. Use the same browser profile and Microsoft-linked GitHub account for both steps. Without a hint, and on macOS/Linux, sign-in goes directly to the standard GitHub flow. No work-email prompt is required. The authorization step opens the default browser using the CLI's web OAuth flow, not a device code. Keeping the same browser profile lets GitHub reuse the session from SSO, so you can approve the GitHub Copilot app without entering a code. If GitHub asks you to sign in again, check that you are using the same browser profile. After authorization, close that tab and return to Skill Recorder; the app verifies access before continuing. Skill Recorder pins Copilot CLI 1.0.78, which supports web OAuth without a terminal, and runs `--no-auto-update login --web-flow` so sign-in does not depend on a different CLI version in the user's auto-update cache. Older bundled versions such as 1.0.71 do not support `--web-flow`. Sign-in can be canceled and times out after five minutes. If browser login fails, the app shows an error and a manual command for the bundled CLI (use PowerShell on Windows). After manual sign-in, retry the analysis yourself. Signing in from a skill or automation builder does not automatically repeat a build or installation. To inspect the script before running it, set install options, update, or uninstall, see [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md). ### Bring your own model Open **AI connection** in Sessions to configure or change your connection. BYOM uses the bundled Copilot SDK/CLI without GitHub login or a Copilot subscription. Model requests go to your selected endpoint and are billed by that provider; BYOM does not mean local/offline processing. | Provider | Required fields | | --- | --- | | Microsoft Foundry / Azure OpenAI (v1) | API key, full `/openai/v1/` base URL, deployment name | | Azure OpenAI (versioned) | API key, resource host without an API path, deployment name, Azure API version | | OpenAI | API key and model ID; the standard base URL is prefilled | | Anthropic | API key and model ID; the standard base URL is prefilled | | Custom OpenAI-compatible | API key, HTTPS base URL, model ID, supported API format | Use a model supporting **image input and tool calling**. **Advanced** selects Responses versus Chat Completions for compatible providers. **Test and save** sends a small, billable synthetic-image/tool test, never a recording. Custom endpoint support depends on actual protocol and model compatibility. Keyless local services and managed-identity authentication are not exposed by this first API-key flow. Keys are protected using the operating system's key storage on Windows 11 (x64/ARM64), macOS, and Ubuntu with a secure desktop keyring. If secure storage is unavailable, the key-entry screen says: > Secure space is unavailable. The Key will be saved in-memory and will be re-asked next time. There is no extra step: BYOM still works for the current app session. Non-secret settings are remembered where possible. **Forget key** removes this app's stored and in-memory credential, not the key at your provider. Finish or cancel active AI work before changing connections. Saved recordings and outputs are preserved, but live conversations are reset. Keys are not included in debug exports. BYOM connection settings and SDK conversation state are stored separately from recordings in app data. Forgetting a key does not erase conversation history. For development, `npm run test:ai` covers configuration, protected/memory-only storage, and connection lifecycle. `npm run test:ai:runtime` exercises the bundled SDK/CLI against a local synthetic provider, including tool-image transport and credential persistence checks. Neither command needs a real API key or sends requests to a paid model. Native key-storage and live-provider release checks are described in [`WINDOWS-VALIDATION.md`](WINDOWS-VALIDATION.md#ai-connection-and-credential-smoke-checks). > ⚠️ **Keep secrets out of your recordings.** Don't record, type, paste, or narrate > passwords, tokens, API keys, or other confidential info. Choosing *Analyze* sends > recording data to your selected AI provider. Skill Recorder reminds you before every recording. > Details in [What gets captured](#what-gets-captured). --- *Everything below is for people who want the details, or want to hack on the code.* ## What gets captured Recording, storage, frame extraction, and optional narration transcription all happen **on your computer**; nothing leaves while you record. Only when you choose **Analyze** does Skill Recorder send the event timeline (window/document titles, URLs, clipboard previews, and terminal commands), extracted screen images, narration text, and bounded terminal-output excerpts requested during analysis to your selected AI provider for processing. When protection is enabled, terminal commands and the complete local terminal transcript participate in the same on-device secret/PII scan before any requested excerpt is returned. The in-app "Records your screen and activity" panel spells out exactly what's collected: - **Window tracking:** active-app / window switches. - **Browser URLs:** the page you're on (macOS). - **Screen video:** recorded by Chromium; low-rate snapshots are kept only when the screen changes or a heartbeat is due. - **Clipboard:** short previews of copied text that tie steps together. - **Narration** *(optional)*: spoken commentary, transcribed **on-device** in any of Whisper's 99 supported languages (a one-time ~252 MB model download on first use). - **Recorded terminal** *(only when opened from the floating recording bar)*: command, cwd, shell, exit status, duration, and the complete terminal output. The transcript has no app-imposed size cap and counts toward the saved session's storage. It captures only the app-owned terminal for that recording—there are no global hooks, profile edits, background command monitors, or observation of existing terminals. > ⚠️ **Please don't capture secrets.** Passwords, access tokens, API keys, credentials, and > other confidential information should never be recorded, typed, pasted, shown, copied, > or narrated during a session. ## Develop from source **For developers changing the code, not for installing the app.** To use Skill Recorder, follow [Install it](#install-it) instead. Requires **Node.js 24**. After checking out a release revision: ```bash npm ci npm run compliance:licenses npm run dev ``` `npm run dev` starts Vite and launches the Electron app with hot-reload; `⌘⇧R` (macOS) / `Ctrl+Shift+R` (Windows) toggles recording from anywhere. Full manual setup, the build and `dist` scripts, and the licensing boundary between local source builds and redistributable packages are in [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md). Maintainers changing versions, dependencies, assets, or releases must follow [`RELEASING.md`](RELEASING.md). ## Evals The Copilot **describer** and **builders** have a fixture-based eval suite; see [`evals/README.md`](evals/README.md). ```bash npm run eval # score the describer against synthetic recordings npm run eval:terminal # score indexed terminal-output use and redaction npm run eval:builder # score the skill/automation generalization ``` ## Documentation - **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md):** install options, inspect-first install, updating, uninstalling, and manual developer setup. - **[RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md):** maintainer release runbook. - **[evals/README.md](evals/README.md):** the describer / builder eval harness. - **[THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md):** licenses for bundled dependencies. ## Security Please don't report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for Microsoft's coordinated-disclosure process and reporting channels. ## Support File bugs and feature requests through **[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/issues)** (search existing issues first to avoid duplicates). Support is limited to the resources described in [`SUPPORT.md`](SUPPORT.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) ## Contributing This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use your contribution. For details, visit [Contributor License Agreements](https://cla.opensource.microsoft.com).
